title: Section of Russia's bridge to Crimea collapses after Ukrainian strike; Kyiv's bridges hit
dek: Ukraine says a road span and arch of the Kerch Strait bridge were destroyed; Russia has halted road and rail traffic and vowed to rebuild, two days before Xi, Trump and Putin meet in Shenzhen.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
A section of the road bridge linking Russia to occupied Crimea lay in the Kerch Strait on Tuesday after a second Ukrainian attack on the 19 km crossing in two days. Ukraine's security service, the SBU, said "one of the metal arches and the automobile span under it were completely destroyed", and that the railway section had also been damaged. Russia's transport ministry said road and rail traffic had been suspended and that, according to preliminary information, no one had been killed on the bridge. By the afternoon, Crimea's Russian-installed head said rail services had resumed and foot passengers could cross by ferry.

The strike came on the same night that Russian ballistic missiles hit two road bridges over the Dnipro in Kyiv, cutting heating and water to parts of the capital, and two days before Russian President Vladimir Putin, US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping are due to meet in Shenzhen, where ending the war is expected to be on the agenda. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said the bridge strike was a response to Russia's attacks on Ukraine's infrastructure.

## What happened

Zelensky described the attack as the "seventh phase of an operation that has been underway for several weeks", during which, he said, Ukrainian forces had "systematically destroyed air defense systems, radars, electronic warfare assets" around the crossing, according to reports. He said Palianytsia drones had struck the road section, while Neptune missiles and Ruta and FP-5 drones were used against the railway section; a Flamingo missile was also used, reports said. Footage he published showed the main road arch and part of the roadway missing between two supports. "Today, parts of it lie on the seabed," the SBU said. None of the Ukrainian claims about weapons or earlier phases can be independently verified.

The attack followed a first strike on the bridge overnight into Monday, when Russia's defence ministry said it had shot down a record 1,336 Ukrainian drones. Russia's defence ministry said on Tuesday that its air defences had destroyed more than 1,400 drones over 23 regions in the latest overnight attack, and Moscow's mayor said more than 800 drones had flown towards the capital, according to reports. Those figures cannot be independently verified.

Sergei Aksyonov, the Russian-installed head of Crimea, wrote on Telegram at 11.06 am IST that "the enemy again attacked the Crimean bridge", that traffic had been suspended, and asked residents and visitors not to travel towards the crossing. In a separate post he said two people had been killed by a Ukrainian drone attack in Crimea's Leninsky district. At 3.48 pm IST he said rail services between Crimea and Taman, on the Russian side of the strait, had resumed and that passengers without vehicles could use the ferry crossing; he made no mention of when road traffic would resume. Authorities in Russia's Krasnodar region said food and warming points had been set up on the approaches to the bridge for stranded drivers.

In Kyiv, Mayor Vitali Klitschko said Russian missiles had hit the Northern and Southern bridges, that the metro had been damaged, and that water and power supplies had been partly cut. Zelensky said four ballistic missiles had been aimed at the Southern Bridge and three at the Northern Bridge, according to reports. Both bridges were still standing but were closed to traffic, and heating mains running across them were damaged, leaving hundreds of apartment buildings on Kyiv's Left Bank without heat, reports said. Ukraine's grid operator, Ukrenergo, announced rolling power cuts. Russia's defence ministry said it had attacked two bridges in Kyiv and that its strikes on Monday night were aimed at military production, including missile and drone plants, and at transport, energy and port infrastructure.

## What Russia says

Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told reporters on Tuesday: "There is no doubt that the bridge will be restored. And it will be even better than before." On Monday he had described the damage from the first strike as minor. He said Deputy Prime Minister Marat Khusnullin, who chairs a government commission on the bridge, had briefed Putin after a meeting of the commission. Russian investigators opened a case into what they called a "terrorist attack", reports said.

Ukraine's presidential sanctions envoy, Vladyslav Vlasiuk, posted a picture of the damaged span with the words "Crimean Bridge. Sanctioned." A Ukrainian military aviation analyst, Andrii Kharuk, said in an interview that restoring the section could take "a year or even longer"; Russia has given no estimate.

## Background

Russia built the bridge after it annexed Crimea from Ukraine in 2014, a move the UN General Assembly declared invalid in a 2014 resolution, and opened the road section in 2018 and the railway in 2019. It is the only fixed road and rail link between Russia and the peninsula and carries fuel, goods and military supplies as well as passengers. Russia also supplies Crimea by ferry and over land through the parts of southern Ukraine it occupies.

The bridge was badly damaged twice before: in October 2022, when a truck exploded on it and parts of the road section fell, and in July 2023, in an attack Ukraine later said it had carried out with sea drones. Neither attack put the crossing out of action for long, according to reports. This time Russian officials have restored rail services but have given no date for reopening the road.

The attacks come as US-mediated talks between Russia and Ukraine in the United Arab Emirates last week ended without a breakthrough, and as Ukraine has stepped up long-range strikes on Russian oil refineries, depots and petrochemical plants this month. Zelensky had said before the Shenzhen meeting that Ukraine would keep striking Russia. China's foreign ministry has said the three-way talks between Xi, Trump and Putin will cover topics of "groundbreaking significance". The Kremlin has said the next round of Russia-Ukraine talks should involve only the US, Russia and Ukraine, without European governments.

## Why it matters for India

India has not taken sides in the war and has called for dialogue. Prime Minister Narendra Modi told the East Asia Summit in Manila on Tuesday that "whether in Ukraine or West Asia, we will continue to support every effort for peace". India remains one of the largest buyers of Russian crude, and an escalation in strikes on energy and transport infrastructure on both sides affects oil and fuel markets that India depends on.

## What happens next

Russia's government commission is expected to set out plans for repairing the road span; for now, passengers without vehicles can take the ferry, and road freight must use the land route through occupied southern Ukraine. Xi, Trump and Putin are due to meet in Shenzhen on Thursday, 19 November, on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit; neither Ukraine nor any European government will be at the table. The Declaration will update this story as Russia and Ukraine give fuller accounts of the damage.

## Key numbers

- 19 km: length of the Kerch Strait bridge, Russia's only fixed link to Crimea
- 1,400+: Ukrainian drones Russia says it destroyed overnight into Tuesday, over 23 regions
- 7: ballistic missiles fired at Kyiv's two road bridges, according to Zelensky
- 19 November: Xi-Trump-Putin meeting in Shenzhen
